subtitle: Gaur: A Capital Unmade by Kings, River and Death

panels.shot: sweeping aerial wide over ruined brick walls on a dry riverbed
panels.action: Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah, Sher Shah Suri and Humayun stand ghostlike above the crumbling gates and mosques of Gaur, the dry scar of the old Ganges channel winding past the dead city.

dialogue.text: This is Gaur in Bengal—the city that died three times: under Mughal guns, Afghan ambition, and a river and epidemic that turned a royal capital into a silent shell.

i18n.hi: ये है बंगाल का गौड़—शहर जो तीन बार मरा: मुगल तोपों से, अफ़ग़ान लालच से, और नदी व महामारी से जो शाही राजधानी को सूना खोल बना गई।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah seated on a terrace above the river
panels.action: Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah sits in quiet majesty on a high palace terrace of Gaur, looking over the broad shimmering channel that once carried the Ganges’ trade past brick mosques and crowded streets.

dialogue.text: When Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah took the Bengal throne, Gaur glittered on the river’s edge, its brick towers and mosques fed by silt, ships and tribute from a fertile delta.

i18n.hi: जब नासिरुद्दीन नसरत शाह ने बंगाल की गद्दी संभाली, गौड़ नदी किनारे चमक रहा था—ईंटी मीनारें, मस्जिदें, जहाज़ और नज़राना, सब उपजाऊ डेल्टा से पोषित।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a court hall, Nasrat Shah in council
panels.action: In Gaur’s audience hall, Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah listens, expression measured, as officers gesture westward on a floor map showing the Ghaghra and Ganges where Babur’s new Mughal power has appeared.

dialogue.text: But beyond the horizon, Babur’s victories at Panipat and Khanwa had birthed a new Mughal power on the Ganges, pressing against Bengal’s western frontier.

i18n.hi: पर दूर अफ़क़ पर, बाबर की पानीपत और खानवा की जीतों ने गंगा पर नई मुगल ताकत को जन्म दिया, जो बंगाल की पश्चिमी सरहद पर दबाव डाल रही थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mughal camp on the Ghaghra riverbank
panels.action: Humayun, young and tense, stands with Babur’s commanders by the Ghaghra’s muddy bank, looking toward the distant Bengal allied Afghan forces across the water as cannon rest beside them.

dialogue.text: In 1529, on the Ghaghra, Babur faced Afghan chiefs aligned with Bengal. His Baburnama records the clash that would check Gaur’s push toward the plains.

i18n.hi: १५२९ में, घाघरा पर, बाबर ने बंगाल से जुड़े अफ़ग़ान सरदारों से सामना किया। बाबरनामा में वो टक्कर दर्ज है जिसने गौड़ की मैदानी बढ़त रोक दी।

panels.shot: dynamic riverwide showing opposing armies across the Ghaghra
panels.action: Armies line both banks of the Ghaghra; Mughal cannon smoke drifts over the water as Afghan banners flutter on the far side, while in the distance Bengal’s contingents watch the fighting unfold.

dialogue.text: Under Mughal guns and manoeuvre, the Afghan coalition broke. Babur’s victory at Ghaghra crippled Bengal’s western ambitions and fixed a new balance on the Ganges.

i18n.hi: मुगल तोपों और चालों के नीचे अफ़ग़ान गठबंधन टूट गया। घाघरा की जीत ने बंगाल की पश्चिमी महत्वाकांक्षा तोड़ दी और गंगा पर नया संतुलन तय कर दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle interior of Gaur court, Nasrat Shah reflective
panels.action: Back in Gaur’s high-ceilinged court, Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah stands by a lattice window, his face half in shadow, hearing news of Ghaghra while scribes record the outcome on palm-leaf and paper.

dialogue.text: Nasrat Shah did not fall in that struggle, yet Ghaghra warned Bengal: Mughal artillery, discipline and diplomacy could reach its borders, and Gaur’s strength had limits.

i18n.hi: नसरत शाह उस जंग में नहीं गिरे, पर घाघरा ने बंगाल को चेतावनी दी: मुगल तोप, अनुशासन और सियासत उसकी सरहद तक पहुँच सकती है, और गौड़ की ताकत सीमित है।

panels.shot: wide shot of bustling Gaur streets and riverfront
panels.action: A busy street in Gaur shows traders, clerks and artisans moving between red-brick mosques, gateways and crowded bazaars, while boats unload grain and cloth along the broad riverside ghats.

dialogue.text: Yet for a time the city thrived—Portuguese visitors later recalled Gaur’s markets, brick monuments and busy riverfront, a capital rooted in water-borne trade.

i18n.hi: फिर भी कुछ समय तक शहर फला-फूला—पुर्तगाली यात्री बाद में गौड़ के बाज़ारों, ईंटी इमारतों और रौनक नदी किनारे को याद करते हैं, पानी की व्यापार पर टिकी राजधानी।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Mughal army approaching Gaur
panels.action: Humayun rides at the head of a Mughal column along the river plain, ranks of cavalry and elephants stretching behind him as Gaur’s lofty walls and gates rise in the hazy distance.

dialogue.text: Then, in 1538, Babur’s son Humayun marched into Bengal. He occupied Gaur and renamed it Jannatabad, folding the old capital into his Mughal dream.

i18n.hi: फिर १५३८ में, बाबर का बेटा हुमायूँ बंगाल में चला आया। उसने गौड़ पर कब्ज़ा किया और इसका नाम जन्नताबाद रखा, पुरानी राजधानी को अपने मुगल ख्वाब में जोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: interior palace shot with Humayun on the throne in Gaur
panels.action: Humayun sits on a temporary throne inside Gaur’s palace, carpets spread over worn stone, as Mughal officers and Bengal nobles stand wary and watchful in a hall hung with old banners.

dialogue.speaker: nasiruddin_nasrat_shah_sher_shah_suri_and_humayu
dialogue.text: Gaur is now Jannatabad, a garden in our empire.

i18n.hi: अब गौड़ नहीं, जन्नताबाद है—हमारे साम्राज्य का बाग़।

panels.shot: tense medium shot of Sher Shah in his Afghan camp
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri, sharp-eyed and deliberate, bends over a rough map by torchlight in his Afghan camp, tracing routes toward Gaur as commanders around him listen in taut silence.

dialogue.text: But Sher Shah Suri was rising from Bihar. Through calculated war and politics, he would drive Humayun from Bengal and from Hindustan itself.

i18n.hi: पर बिहार से शेरशाह सूरी उठ रहा था। नपी-तुली जंग और सियासत से वो हुमायूँ को बंगाल और खुद हिन्दुस्तान से भी उखाड़ फेंकेगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Sher Shah’s forces entering Gaur
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri rides through Gaur’s gate at the head of Afghan troops, the Mughal standards gone, local soldiers standing aside as the city’s crowded lanes watch the new ruler pass.

dialogue.text: Humayun’s hold on Gaur proved brief. Sher Shah’s advance displaced him, drawing Bengal into his short-lived Sur empire and ending Mughal rule there—for a time.

i18n.hi: गौड़ पर हुमायूँ की पकड़ थोड़ी ही रही। शेरशाह की बढ़त ने उसे हटाया, बंगाल को उसके अल्पकालिक सूर साम्राज्य में खींच लिया और कुछ समय को मुगल राज ख़त्म कर दिया।

panels.shot: montage-style wide of Afghan and Mughal hosts facing off
panels.action: Across open country beyond Bengal, an Afghan army under Sur banners faces a later Mughal host, dust hanging over lines of cavalry as the two powers contest the eastern plains.

dialogue.text: In the years after, Afghan and Mughal struggles tore through the region. By 1576, Mughal victory ended Bengal’s independent sultanate and fixed imperial rule over its lands.

i18n.hi: आगे के बरसों में अफ़ग़ान और मुगल टकराव ने इलाके को चीर डाला। १५७६ तक मुगल जीत ने बंगाल की आज़ाद सल्तनत खत्म कर दी और उस पर साम्राज्य की पकड़ बैठा दी।

panels.shot: serene but ominous aerial of the Ganges changing course
panels.action: From high above the delta, the old channel by Gaur lies narrower and dull while a new, wider arm of the Ganges gleams far to the north, carrying most of the water and traffic away.

dialogue.text: Yet military defeat was only one blow. Environmental historians note that the Ganges’ main course shifted away from Gaur, pulling trade and fresh silt from its doorstep.

i18n.hi: पर सैनिक हार अकेला वार नहीं थी। पर्यावरण के इतिहासकार बताते हैं कि गंगा की मुख्य धारा गौड़ से दूर हट गई, व्यापार और नया गारा उसके दरवाज़े से खिसक गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of stagnant water and abandoned ghats in Gaur
panels.action: Steps of Gaur’s riverfront ghats descend now into shallow, stagnant water, boats pulled up and rotting, while simple huts replace once-busy warehouses along the bank.

dialogue.text: As the river wandered, channels near Gaur silted and stagnated. Boats chose deeper streams elsewhere, and the city’s lifeline of movement and commerce thinned.

i18n.hi: जैसे नदी भटकी, गौड़ के पास की धाराएँ भरकर दलदल बन गईं। नावें गहरी धारा की ओर मुड़ गईं और शहर की आवाजाही और कारोबार की नस पतली पड़ गई।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of a house with sick bodies and anxious faces
panels.action: Inside a modest brick house in Gaur, a family sits in fear beside several motionless figures on mats, while outside, a cart creaks past carrying more covered bodies toward the outskirts.

dialogue.text: Portuguese reports and later memory speak of a terrible epidemic. People died in great numbers, so fast that streets emptied and fear seeped into every doorway.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली बयान और बाद की याद में भयानक महामारी का ज़िक्र है। लोग इतनी तेज़ी से, इतने ज़्यादा मरे कि गलियाँ खाली हो गईं और हर चौखट पर डर उतर आया।

panels.shot: wide shot of partially deserted Gaur streets
panels.action: A once-crowded street in Gaur lies half-deserted; shuttered shops, stray cattle and a few hurried figures mark a city whose brick facades now bear cracks and creeping plants.

dialogue.text: The pathogen cannot be named with certainty, but the pattern of sudden, mass death broke households, labour and confidence. The city’s decline sped beyond the reach of rulers.

i18n.hi: रोग की पहचान पक्की नहीं, पर अचानक, बड़ी मौतों के इस ढर्रे ने घर, मेहनत और भरोसा तोड़ दिया। शहर की गिरावट शासकों की पकड़ से बाहर तेज़ हो गई।

panels.shot: melancholic wide of ruined mosque and encroaching jungle
panels.action: A grand brick mosque at Gaur stands roofless, arches broken, its courtyard filled with grass and small trees, as jungle foliage presses close around its fading walls.

dialogue.text: By the time Mughal authority settled over Bengal, Gaur was already slipping away. Brick mosques, gates and towers were left to crumble, their materials reused in humbler buildings.

i18n.hi: जब तक मुगल हकूमत बंगाल पर जमकर बैठी, गौड़ पहले ही फिसल चुका था। ईंटी मस्जिदें, फाटक, मीनारें ढहने को छोड़ दी गईं, उनकी ईंटें मामूली मकानों में फिर से जुड़ गईं।

panels.shot: close-up of weathered inscription stone half-buried
panels.action: A carved inscription slab from Gaur lies half-buried in earth and roots, its letters worn but still visible, catching a shaft of late sunlight in the encroaching shade.

dialogue.text: Archaeological surveys today trace Gaur’s outline through ruins and reused stone, reading in its decay a story of shifting rivers, abandoned routes and forgotten patronage.

i18n.hi: आज पुरातत्त्व सर्वेक्षण खंडहरों और पुनः इस्तेमाल पत्थर से गौड़ की शक्ल पढ़ते हैं, उसकी टूटन में बदलती नदियाँ, सूनी राहें और भूली सरपरस्ती की कहानी देखते हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the three rulers’ silhouettes over Gaur’s ruins
panels.action: Silhouettes of Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah, Sher Shah Suri and Humayun stand above the overgrown remains of Gaur’s walls and mosques, the dry riverbed curving away under a vast sky.

dialogue.text: Gaur’s three deaths—by Mughal and Afghan power, by epidemic, by a river’s slow turn—remind us that even the greatest capitals rest on fragile ecologies of water, health and trade.

i18n.hi: गौड़ की तीन मौतें—मुगल और अफ़ग़ान ताकत से, महामारी से, और नदी की धीमी मोड़ से—याद दिलाती हैं कि सबसे बड़ी राजधानियाँ भी पानी, सेहत और व्यापार की नाज़ुक दुनिया पर टिकी होती हैं।

title_i18n.en: The City That Died Three Times

subtitle_i18n.en: Gaur: A Capital Unmade by Kings, River and Death
